top3.headline: Anthropic launches the roadshow for its proposed IPO
top3.whyItMatters: A core AI vendor going public means more disclosure on the business you depend on.

top3.headline: One sentence makes Fable 5.2 far more willing to clean up code
top3.whyItMatters: Small prompt changes shift agent behavior a lot, so standardize the ones that work.

top3.headline: Amazon team replaced Sonnet with a small model at 98% less cost
top3.whyItMatters: Routine agent tasks can often run on small models, freeing budget for hard work.

items.title: Anthropic launches the roadshow for its proposed IPO
items.takeaway: Anthropic says an SEC registration statement is filed but not yet effective.
items.soWhat: A core enterprise AI vendor is heading to public markets, which brings public disclosure.

image.alt: @AnthropicAI on X: Anthropic launches the roadshow for its proposed IPO

items.title: Meng To builds a landing page with Opus 5.5 and Lottie AI
items.takeaway: The animated card, logo and menu icons are Lottie files, not videos; the card is 51 KB.
items.soWhat: AI tools now produce rich, lightweight motion design that loads fast on any site.

items.title: Matt Pocock: agents game metrics, so PR counts mislead
items.takeaway: An opinion post with no data: he argues tracking pull request counts breaks once agents write the code.
items.soWhat: Measure agent-era engineering by outcomes, not by the volume of pull requests.

items.title: Geoffrey Huntley: at each model drop, reread the card, prune skills
items.takeaway: His checklist: always read the model card and consider removing old skills and AGENTS.md files.
items.soWhat: Old agent instructions can hold new models back, so review them with every upgrade.

items.title: Amazon ticket labeling matched Sonnet at 98% lower cost
items.takeaway: Vendor blog from the Strands Agents team: a small Strands Decider build on one GPU replaced Claude Sonnet 4.6 for internal labeling.
items.soWhat: Narrow, high-volume agent tasks may not need frontier models, so test small ones first.

items.title: Anthropic: 'This codebase is yours' makes Fable 5.2 refactor more
items.takeaway: In Anthropic's tests the line led the model to merge repeated code in about half of tries, versus under a tenth without it.
items.soWhat: Ownership framing in prompts measurably changes agent behavior; add it to your team's coding setup.

items.title: ThePrimeagen: Opus 5.5 orchestrating DeepSeek workers felt fast
items.takeaway: He called the pairing awesome, while a pipeline QA test gave only a moderate speedup.
items.soWhat: A strong planner with cheap, fast workers is becoming a common agent pattern worth piloting.

items.title: Theo: the $200 Claude plan buys far less Fable than Opus
items.takeaway: He estimates about $15,000 of Opus 5.5 versus about $3,000 of Fable per month, with Fable capped at half the weekly limit.
items.soWhat: Reserve the premium model for planning and keep heavy building on cheaper models.

related.name: @kloss_xyz: plan with Fable, build with Opus

items.title: Lyn Alden: markets shrugged off Nvidia's scandal, for now
items.takeaway: She notes stocks rose over 2% while Nvidia fell less than 5%, and flags more risk ahead.
items.soWhat: Investors so far price Huang's scandal as company risk, not a threat to the AI trade.

image.alt: @LynAldenContact on X: Lyn Alden: markets shrugged off Nvidia's scandal, for now

items.title: Verge: what is known about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting Huang
items.takeaway: Stratechery says the story got worse today, and The Atlantic calls it a scandal at the center of the economy.
items.soWhat: Leadership risk at the top AI chip supplier keeps growing; watch your supply exposure.

items.title: Theo: Fable 5.2 built a project in 76 minutes for $42
items.takeaway: He says the result was not significantly better than Opus 5.5, especially for the price.
items.soWhat: Test new flagships on your own work before paying a premium for marginal gains.

items.title: OpenAI builds Control Room to halt risky research workloads fast
items.takeaway: It tracks every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for training and evals, from one place.
items.soWhat: If you run agents at scale, you need one place to see and stop them.

items.title: ClaudeDevs maps when to use Fable, Opus, Sonnet or Haiku
items.takeaway: The guide also covers adjusting effort before switching models, and running subagents on smaller models to save cost.
items.soWhat: Tune effort first and put subagents on smaller models; that is where agent costs fall.

items.title: MIT Tech Review: data center backlash may be about electricity
items.takeaway: MIT Technology Review argues the backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity.
items.soWhat: Expect local power costs to shape pushback on new AI data centers.

items.title: Ethan Mollick: Fable 5.2 is 'almost' AGI, in a jagged way
items.takeaway: He says its remaining gaps are no longer simple errors or hallucinations.
items.soWhat: Judge the new flagship on real expert work in your business, not on benchmarks.

items.title: Anthropic ships Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, up to 30% faster
items.takeaway: Same model under two names; Fable adds cyber and bio safeguards so all users get it. $8/$40 per million tokens.
items.soWhat: Anthropic itself says start with Opus 5.5 and use Fable 5.2 as advisor or orchestrator.

related.name: Ethan Mollick: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI

items.title: Meta's Muse Ember matches GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on price
items.takeaway: Simon Willison: $0.10 per million input and $0.50 output tokens for short prompts; Fable 5.2 costs about 80x more.
items.soWhat: A cheap model built for tool calls and routing could lower the cost of agent subtasks.

items.title: Nancy Pelosi's replacement is ready to regulate AI
items.takeaway: MIT Technology Review reports that Nancy Pelosi's replacement is ready to regulate AI.
items.soWhat: Post-midterm Congress may push AI rules harder; plan compliance before bills arrive.

items.title: Nathan Benaich: defenders need open cyber models too
items.takeaway: He says Hugging Face found API guardrails slowed an intrusion probe and used a self-hosted open model.
items.soWhat: Closed-model guardrails can block your own security team; keep an open-model option for incidents.

items.title: Meng To rebuilds his apartment as a walkable 3D web scene
items.takeaway: Built with Opus 5.5 in three.js for tutorial videos: walkable in the browser, adjustable lighting, render styles, every object defined in code.
items.soWhat: Designers can now build interactive 3D spaces from prompts, without a 3D modeling team.

items.title: Lyn Alden: Japan's real market force is its overseas cash
items.takeaway: Alden says Japan's quiet Godzilla is not the carry trade but its net international investment position, from pensions to private investors.
items.soWhat: Watch Japan's pension and private money abroad, not just the carry trade, for global market risk.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin: a data center slowdown looks net good
items.takeaway: Vitalik argues algorithmic progress lets today's data centers match bigger ones within about four years, buying time to harden against cyber and bio risks.
items.soWhat: Opposition to data centers now has a capability-neutral case that investors and boards will hear.
